title: Altman pitches Musk on a 'Manhattan Project for AI'
description: Altman emails Musk: 'we could structure it so that the tech belongs to the world via some sort of nonprofit but the people working on it get startup-like compensation if it works.' Musk replies: 'Probably worth a conversation.'

title: Founding terms emailed; Musk: 'Agree on all'
description: Altman: 'The technology would be owned by the foundation and used "for the good of the world"… safety should be a first-class requirement.' Musk: 'Agree on all'.

title: Brockman 'bootstrap' email
description: Brockman to Musk: 'I hope for us to enter the field as a neutral group looking to collaborate widely… (I think that's the best way to bootstrap ourselves into being a leading research institution.)' — plaintiffs cite this as evidence the nonprofit framing was strategic.

title: OpenAI publicly launches as a 501(c)(3)
description: OpenAI announced as a $1B-pledged nonprofit AI research lab. Musk co-authors the public statements — a fact later used to dismiss his California false-advertising claim (Dkt #163 p.7).

title: Musk tells Jensen Huang OpenAI is a nonprofit
description: 'OpenAI is unaffiliated with Tesla, is a nonprofit company by me and a few others with the goal of developing safe AGI (and hopefully not paving the road to hell with good intentions).' (Ex. 70, read at trial 042826TT.txt:5623)

citations.snippet: OpenAI is unaffiliated with Tesla, is a nonprofit…

title: Musk's first wire to OpenAI
description: First of dozens of wires that totaled $44.56M between May 2016 and June 2020 (FAC ¶424). Largest single wire: $16,028,500 on Jan 1, 2017.

title: Microsoft compute deal — Musk: 'not Microsoft's marketing bitch'
description: Microsoft proposed $60M of compute for $10M with an 'evangelize' obligation. Musk: 'Would be worth way more than $50M not to seem like Microsoft's marketing bitch.' Final deal: $50M with no evangelism, no strings.

title: First documentary signal of for-profit redesign
description: Sutskever bi-weekly update circulated to Musk lists 'Designing the for-profit structure' as ongoing work.

title: Musk to Zilis: 'I've had enough'
description: Privately, Musk: 'This is very annoying. Please encourage them to go start a company. I've had enough.' Plaintiffs frame this as the start of the for-profit push; defense uses the same period to show Musk himself was advocating a 'standard C corp with a parallel nonprofit'.

title: Musk's ultimatum; Sutskever/Brockman push back on 'unilateral absolute control'
description: Musk: 'continue with OpenAI as a non-profit. I will no longer fund OpenAI until you have made a firm commitment to stay or I'm just being a fool…' Sutskever/Brockman counter that Musk's proposed structure 'provides you with a path where you end up with unilateral absolute control over the AGI'.

title: Altman: 'i remain enthusiastic about the non-profit structure!'
description: Single sentence reaffirmation; the linchpin of plaintiffs' fraud and constructive-fraud claims. Defense will argue this was truthful at the time.

title: Zilis to Musk: 'Great with keeping non-profit'
description: Zilis reports from Altman: 'Structure: Great with keeping non-profit and continuing to support it.' Musk continued funding for nearly three more years (~$10.275M after this date).

title: Musk resigns from the OpenAI board
description: Resignation effective February 2018, after Altman/Brockman/Sutskever refused Musk's demands for 'unequivocal initial control' of a for-profit OpenAI or absorption into Tesla. Plaintiffs treat this as 'sidelined'; defense treats this as 'walked away'.

title: Musk to OpenAI leadership: 'zero percent: not 1 percent'
description: DX 853: Musk's probability assessment of OpenAI being relevant 'without a dramatic change in execution and resources is zero percent.'

citations.snippet: My probability assessment of OpenAI being relevant to DeepMind/Google… is zero percent: not 1 percent.

title: OpenAI launches the capped-profit OpenAI L.P.
description: Press release announces a for-profit subsidiary with capped returns. Altman: 'we did this in a way where all investors are clear that they should never expect a profit.' Musk's reply asks Altman to 'be explicit that [Musk] ha[d] no financial interest in the for-profit arm of OpenAI'.

title: Microsoft's first $1B investment
description: Microsoft enters strategic partnership; capped-return structure tied to commercial product revenue. Plaintiffs allege exclusive cloud arrangement begins here. Microsoft's MSJ: 'arm's-length negotiations between sophisticated parties.'

title: Musk's last quarterly contribution
description: Final regular wire ends the multi-year donation pattern. On cross: Q: 'When did you give your last penny?' A: 'I think that was in 2020.' (043026TT.txt:3591)

title: OpenAI solicits a 'final one-time donation' of $570,000 from Musk
description: Cited by plaintiffs as evidence OpenAI was still soliciting Musk as a charitable donor in 2020 — relevant to the Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §17510.8 fiduciary-duty theory.

title: Musk's 'captured by Microsoft' tweet
description: PX 251: 'OpenAI is essentially captured by Microsoft.' Defense: this is the date the statute of limitations begins; plaintiffs: it expressed unease, not fraud-discovery.

citations.snippet: OpenAI is essentially captured by Microsoft.

title: Microsoft's $10B expansion
description: Reported $10B Microsoft investment in OpenAI; Musk testified this is when he 'finally came to the conclusion… that OpenAI was really going to become a profit-maximizing, closed-source organization' — the moment he says he became sure the charity had been looted.

title: xAI Corp. founded; Hoffman resigns from OpenAI board
description: Musk launches xAI Corp. as a Nevada public benefit corporation. Hoffman resigns from OpenAI's board around the same period — important for the later Section 8 standing analysis.

title: Altman removed by the OpenAI nonprofit board
description: Toner, McCauley, D'Angelo, and Sutskever vote to remove Altman; Murati named interim CEO. Microsoft hires Altman within days. Within five days, Altman is reinstated and the board is reconstituted.

title: Reconstituted OpenAI board; Templeton joins as observer
description: Microsoft's Deannah Templeton seated as a non-voting observer of OpenAI Inc.'s board.

title: Templeton resigns from OpenAI board observer role
description: Departure cited in PI ruling as predating the FAC by four months — fatal to the Section 8 standing theory.

title: Musk files the original federal complaint
description: Original complaint, 84 pages, names Altman, Brockman, OpenAI corporate web, and Aestas entities. 26 causes of action.

title: OpenAI moves to dismiss the original complaint
description: Motion to dismiss filed (Dkt #25); plaintiffs respond by filing the FAC, mooting the motion.

title: First Amended Complaint (FAC); Zilis & xAI added
description: Verified FAC adds Shivon Zilis (derivative) and xAI Corp. as plaintiffs; expands antitrust theories.

title: Plaintiffs move for preliminary injunction
description: PI motion seeks four orders, most importantly to enjoin OpenAI's for-profit conversion and the alleged 'fund-no-competitors' covenant.

title: Preliminary-injunction hearing
description: 108-page transcript at #109. Court signals the charitable-trust theory is a 'toss-up' but other claims fall short.

title: Musk's $97.375B Letter of Intent
description: LOI to acquire OpenAI's nonprofit assets for $97.375B; press leak to the Wall Street Journal. The court treats the LOI itself as connected to the litigation; the public media campaign as not protected. The spine of OpenAI's surviving counterclaims.

title: Court denies preliminary injunction
description: Likelihood of success on the charitable trust 'a toss-up'; antitrust claims rejected for lack of admissible evidence; xAI 'could not provide a single declaration from an investor'. Court offers an expedited fall-2025 trial on the trust claim alone.

title: Motion-to-dismiss hearing on the FAC
description: Hearing transcript at #144; the court's questions preview the May 1, 2025 ruling.

title: OpenAI files Answer + Counterclaim against Musk and xAI
description: First counterclaim: harassment campaign theory; the LOI characterized as a 'sham bid' and 'stunt'. Tells the case as a competitive-interference story: 'Musk could not tolerate seeing such success for an enterprise he had abandoned and declared doomed.' (¶6)

title: Court partially grants and partially denies MTD of FAC
description: Express contract DISMISSED w/o leave. Implied-in-fact contract SURVIVES. Constructive fraud + fraud SURVIVE. Charitable trust SURVIVES. Microsoft survives on tortious interference and aiding-and-abetting fiduciary duty. RICO §1962(c) dismissed with leave; (a) and (b) without leave. Derivative claims dismissed without leave.

title: Second Amended Complaint
description: Drops Zilis as a plaintiff; xAI remains. Drops some defendants and adds Aestas back. Re-pleads RICO and the implied covenant.

title: Court strikes 16 of 55 affirmative defenses
description: Order on motion to strike chastises both sides: 'the parties have repeatedly over-litigated this case… The Court will not waste precious judicial resources on the parties' gamesmanship.'

title: Order on plaintiffs' MTD of counterclaims; SAC screening
description: Counterclaims SURVIVE: UCL (fraudulent + unfair prongs) and tortious interference with prospective economic advantage. SAC repleaded RICO §1962(c) and implied covenant DISMISSED without leave. Litigation privilege protects the LOI; not the press campaign.

title: Amended counterclaims
description: OpenAI files Amended Counterclaims after the August 12 ruling.

title: Pretrial schedule modified; MSJ pre-filing conference relieved
description: Court relieves parties from the MSJ pre-filing conference and resets dates: MSJs Oct 17, opposition Nov 7, reply Nov 21, MSJ argument Jan 7, 2026; trial Mar 30, 2026 (later moved to Apr 27, 2026 for jury selection).

title: OpenAI and Microsoft file MSJs
description: OpenAI MSJ: time-bar on fraud claims; no actionable misrepresentation; settler standing fails because donations routed through DAFs/YC.org; statute of limitations expired 2022. Microsoft MSJ: arm's-length partnership; no conventional equity; no diversion of partnership benefits.

title: Sutskever third-party discovery fight
description: Magistrate orders Sutskever to comply with discovery by Nov 5; Sutskever's motion to stay denied as moot Oct 31 (#348).

title: Plaintiffs' MSJ opposition (last entry in archive)
description: Plaintiffs argue settler standing under Restatement (Third) of Trusts §94, statutory standing under Cal. Corp. Code §5142(a)(4), and Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §17510.8. Cite Musk's 2023 testimony — that he 'finally came to the conclusion' OpenAI was profit-maximizing — as the discovery date that defeats the limitations defense.

title: Trial begins; jury selected
description: Nine-person jury empaneled; trial-wiki day-1 entries note overflow rooms and the judge's brief Twitter colloquy with Musk on social-media discipline. Two surviving claims for the jury: breach of charitable trust and restitution under unjust enrichment.

title: Openings; Musk direct begins
description: Molo: 'we're here today because the defendants stole a charity… The museum store can't loot the museum, sell the Picassos, and pocket the profits.' Savitt: 'Mr. Musk's lawsuit is a pageant of hypocrisy.' Cohen: 'Mr. Musk never picked up the phone to say, you can't do this.'

title: Court frames the case scope
description: 'This is not a trial on the safety risks of artificial intelligence… The question here is whether there was a breach of charitable trust.' Birchall takes the stand; testifies on contributions, Pioneer Building, and the LOI.

title: Birchall LOI testimony struck; Toberoff sanctioned; jury-instructions ruling
description: Court grants motion to strike Birchall's LOI testimony ('this gentleman had no personal knowledge'). Court rules §17510.6 controls over §17510.8 under Cohen v. Kabbalah Centre and that there is 'no separate cause of action for unjust enrichment' under California Supreme Court precedent — only restitution. Plaintiffs' attempt to redirect any restitution to a charity rather than to Musk personally rebuffed: 'I could also just not give an advisory opinion on this topic.'

title: Day 6: Russell completes; Brockman adverse direct begins
description: Stuart Russell finishes as plaintiffs' AI-safety expert; cross by Frentzen drew out he had never previously testified as an expert. Greg Brockman takes the stand for adverse direct by Robert Kry — first time the OpenAI President has testified under oath in this case. Cross covers Brockman's ~$30B equity stake (paid in $0); a $10M side-payment from Altman in 2017 documented in PX-350 (Birchall→Musk: 'naturally, Greg is going to have greater allegiance towards Sam'); undisclosed Cerebras ownership during 2017 merger talks; the self-dealing roster from PX-390 (Stripe ~$471M; CoreWeave with ~$22.4B in 2025 OpenAI counterparty deals; Helion ties); the Microsoft funding ladder ($1B/2019, $2B/2021 [previously unannounced], $10B/2023); the 2025 PBC conversion bringing OpenAI's post-money valuation to ~$840B with IPO under exploration. Headline documentary moment: PX-161 — Brockman's own 11/06/2017 journal: 'it'd partially be wrong to steal the nonprofit from him. To convert to B Corp without him. They'd be pretty morally bankrupt.' Friendly examination by Steven Molo begins late in the session and continues at the cutoff. Court (sustaining the dollar-value line of questioning): 'the dollar value goes to motive… Impact, credibility, and motive.' Citations are to the live trial transcript and may renumber against the official 050426TT.txt when published.
